content.text:
I've updated `0.svg`. The original file was an empty `<svg>` element with no content and no `viewBox`, so there was nothing to improve as such. The only hint was the filename, so I made it a clean digit **0** in the usual 24×24 icon format:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" role="img">
  <title>Zero</title>
  <rect x="6" y="3" width="12" height="18" rx="6" ry="7.5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
</svg>
```

- **Scales to any size:** the `viewBox` sets a coordinate system, so the image resizes cleanly. I left out a fixed width and height on purpose.
- **Shape:** it's a rounded rectangle with oval corners, which gives an oval with slightly flat sides, like the zero in many modern fonts. A plain ellipse tends to look more mechanical.
- **Crisp at 24px:** the outline is 2 units thick and its edges fall on whole pixels at 24px, so it doesn't blur at that size.
- **Matches surrounding text:** `currentColor` makes it take the text colour when placed inline in a page. Opened on its own, it shows as black.
- **Accessible:** `role="img"` and the `<title>` give screen readers a name to read out.

**I haven't seen it rendered or checked it with a validator.** The rendering and checking tools (`resvg`, `xmllint`, `svgo`) needed permission, which nobody could grant in this session. I also couldn't use scratch space outside this folder. I worked out the shape by hand instead. To look at it yourself, run `qlmanage -p 0.svg`.
